# Hypertension: a real metagenomics case study

Apply the workflow to **LiJ_2017**, a human stool shotgun metagenomics study available through curatedMetagenomicData. Complete [Required setup](../../00-setup.qmd) and synthetic practice first.

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
## Our question

How do species composition, Shannon diversity and annotated pathway profiles vary between Control and hypertension (HTN) samples in these processed profiles?
:::

## What you are working with

The main example includes **140 samples from 140 distinct subject IDs: 41 Control and 99 HTN**. Both abundance tables contain the same sample accessions.

| Input | Verified contents | Measurement |
|---|---|---|
| Sample metadata | 140 samples with group, subject ID and source identifiers | One row per sample |
| Taxonomic abundance | 440 species-level features | Source percentages; approximately 100 per sample |
| Functional features | 483 named, unstratified MetaCyc pathways | HUMAnN source relative abundances |

The full curated cohort has **196 samples: 41 Control, 56 pre-hypertension (pHTN), 99 HTN**. The main lesson excludes pHTN to keep the first real-data comparison focused. All 196 samples remain available in `data/hypertension-all-groups/` for an optional extension.

::: {.callout-important}
## What this analysis can support

These are real processed profiles, not raw reads. This descriptive human comparison does not establish statistical significance or causation. Age, sex and BMI are unavailable in the pinned curated metadata; this workflow does not adjust for confounding. Pathway abundance describes annotated functional potential, not directly measured activity.
:::

## Study and data sources

The original human cohort and additional experimental work are described by [Li et al. (2017)](https://doi.org/10.1186/s40168-016-0222-x). This lesson analyses the human profiles reprocessed by [curatedMetagenomicData](https://waldronlab.io/curatedMetagenomicData/), using the 2021-10-14 abundance resources. It does not reproduce the original paper's entire analysis or its animal experiments.
